ELC00.title: Language and runtime
ELC00.text: Raised by the compiler and while a program runs: syntax, undeclared variables, values that don't fit their type, division by zero, list limits, call depth. A compile that gives any message of severity 20 or more makes no program; ELC0008 is a warning and the program is still created.

ELC01.title: Commands
ELC01.text: A command that doesn't exist, a required parameter left out, a value a parameter doesn't take, or a command used where it can't run (on the command line, in a batch job or in a program). ELC0108 and ELC0110 are the completion messages of `CALL` on the command line.

ELC02.title: Objects
ELC02.text: Libraries, members, programs and system values: not found, already there, read-only, locked, out of storage, and the completion messages of the library, member and program commands.

ELC03.title: Jobs
ELC03.text: Batch jobs, schedule entries and triggers. ELC0303 (ended by `ENDJOB` or the job screens) and ELC0310 (its job host was unloaded or lost power) have severity 40: they're recorded when the job is ended from outside, so the program gets no chance to catch them.

ELC04.title: Security
ELC04.text: A Firewall permission or an OS authority the user doesn't have, and failed sign-ons.

ELC12.title: Inventory and storage
ELC12.text: Items not in the network, not enough of an item, storage full, ambiguous item names, recalls from tape and resource types.

ELC13.title: Devices
ELC13.text: Devices that aren't found, are offline or don't support a command; printers, diskettes, Display Panels, images and Arcforge machines.

ELC14.title: Crafting
ELC14.text: No Scheduler, no recipe, missing ingredients, or a crafting job that isn't found.

ELC15.title: PLCs
ELC15.text: PLC modules, programs and the commands a PLC with no network can't run.

ELC22.title: Database files
ELC22.text: Reading and writing records (ELC2201 to ELC2209), definition errors when a physical file is compiled (ELC2220 to ELC2228), and the file commands' completion messages and errors (ELC2230 to ELC2247).

ELC24.title: Lights, sirens and speakers
ELC24.text: Cage Light levels, Speaker audio files, web audio, notes and MIDI files.

ELC25.title: Schematics and craft steps
ELC25.text: Schematic holders, a crafting job's planned steps, and schematics moved to a Rack Schematic Console's drawer.

ELC26.title: Routing, exchanges and the directory
ELC26.text: Routers, routes, neighbours, ACLs, Exchange Switch members and the Directory Server.

ELC27.title: Chassis and optical
ELC27.text: Chassis Switches, Blade Enclosures, Optical Transport Shelves, spans, channels and protection switching.

USR.title: Your own messages
USR.text: Sent with `SNDPGMMSG`: the default ID is USR0001, and `MSGID(USRnnnn)` picks another. The text is whatever `MSG()` says. `MSGTYPE(*INFO)` (the default) only logs it; `MSGTYPE(*ESCAPE)` makes it an error of severity 30 that ends the program unless a `MONMSG` catches it. `MONMSG MSGID(USR0000)` catches every USR message, and `MONMSG MSGID(USR0100)` the ones from USR0100 to USR0199. `MONMSG MSGID(ELC0000)` catches them too, since it catches every message.
